sections.html:
The Atabo red pike cichlid, Lugubria lugubris, is a large pike cichlid from rivers in Suriname, Guyana and Brazil. Colourful when small, it quickly grows into an aggressive adult of up to 40 cm and will eat any fish small enough to be considered food. Pairs are difficult to form because males become increasingly aggressive as they mature, and prospective mates are often killed.

  • Needs 27 °C or warmer
  • Needs a very large tank
Has been recorded from the Rio Corantijn in Suriname, Rio Essequibo in Guyana, Rio Negro and Rio Uatumã in Brazil and Rio Branco in both Brazil and Guyana.

• Standard length: 40 cm SL
  • Aquarium base: 180 × 60 cm
  • Volume: ~972 litres (180 × 60 × 90 cm)

Sand substrate is recommended. This species is likely to dig and arrange the decor to suit itself. Some rockwork should be provided to form caves as pikes like to have an area to which they can retreat. Plants should be robust, ideally potted or rooted to bogwood.

Feed a varied diet including a good quality cichlid pellet or flake, live or frozen foods such as bloodworm or brine shrimp, meaty foods such as prawn and mussel and vegetable matter in the form of spirulina or algae wafers.

Can be aggressive, especially towards conspecifics. May be kept with other large cichlids or as a species only setup. Likely to eat any fish small enough to be considered food - and they have big mouths!
Male has white stripe on the dorsal fin. Females are more colourful.

Very few reports of breeding in captivity. Believed to be a cave spawner. Excellent parental care is exhibited. Can be difficult to form a pair due to the increasing aggression from the male as the fish mature. Prospective mates are often killed.
An attractive and colourful fish when small, this species quickly grows into a large aggressive adult, requiring a large tank.
